title: GHAPPIER Malware Hijacks 65 GitHub Repositories to Deploy Self-Deleting Backdoor
content_md: A supply-chain attack linked to the GHAPPIER malware campaign compromised the legitimate npm package @dforge-core/dforge-mcp and briefly distributed a self-deleting backdoor. The incident began on September 9, 2026, when an attacker used the maintainer account of the package for about 105 minutes. The attacker already had permission to push code to the repository’s main branch when the intrusion started. The exact method used to obtain this access remains unknown. Researchers believe the most likely scenario is that a developer device was infected by a malicious browser extension or npm package . Such malware may have stolen cached Git credentials, allowing attackers to use the maintainer’s identity across unrelated GitHub repositories. During the short access window, the threat actor added a remote code loader to the project. They also changed three lines of code so every push to the main branch launched the release workflow. GHAPPIER Hijacks GitHub Repositories Fourteen minutes later, the attacker modified the workflow again to enable unattended publishing. The malicious package was released as version 0.2.21 and remained the latest npm version for 35 minutes and 38 seconds. The maintainer later reverted the changes and published a clean version, 0.2.22. However, researchers warned that simply withdrawing the malicious release may not fully protect users who installed version 0.2.21. The malicious npm release included valid provenance records.
